premises_refuted: R-A (LOUD - ISSUE #538's OWN HEADLINE FRAMING IS WRONG): #538 calls the 0/10-vs-1/10 boundary 'incoherent' and says 'a strictly worse benchmark gets the quieter label'. The ordering is DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED and DEFENSIBLE - it is ordered by EVIDENCE OF ACHIEVABILITY, not by badness. design_docs/implemented/v1_0_0/m-nightly-flake-guard.md:263-270: 'only a p-hat == 0 window (GAP, never-passed/already-failing) is excluded - that is gap-finder territory, same as today. This makes the worst case provable: no benchmark THAT HAS EVER PASSED goes unpaged past its 3rd consecutive failing night.' A 0/10 bench has never been observed green on this model, so there is no evidence it is achievable -> benchmark-design/capability question, and it DOES get a channel (the GAP --type note at :557-570, explicitly 'Gap-finder candidates'). A 1/10 bench HAS been observed green -> a sustained all-fail run is worth a triage slot. CONSEQUENCE FOR SCOPE: GAP stays exempt and M1.6 adds a test that LOCKS the exemption with a comment citing D2, so a future reader who trusts #538's framing cannot silently widen it. The real defect in #538 is narrower than its own title: the escalated verdict ASSERTS SOMETHING FALSE, nothing more. That narrowing is what keeps this sprint at 0.9d.

R-B (LOUD - THE CONTROLLER'S PROPOSED BODY WORDING IS ITSELF FALSE, same error class it fixes): the handoff proposes the body say 'never green in the window'. Escalation is LABEL-AGNOSTIC across SUSPECTED-FLAKE AND INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY (:349, `label not in {'REGRESSION','GAP'}`; flake-guard :265-267 revised it that way in quorum round 1 deliberately). A bench with ONE prior night at 2/2 is INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY (min_nights=2) and escalates after 3 all-fail nights - and that bench WAS GREEN. tools/test_nightly_classify.py:733-747 (test_new_benchmark_timeline) is exactly this shape. The wording must be the statement true in EVERY escalation case: 'failed all trials for N consecutive nights; the prior window is NOT SOLID (X/Y passes), so this is not a certified fresh break - triage as sustained failure / capability gap.' No 'never green'. No 'solid-window break'. M2.2 pins it with a body-text test.

R-C (CORRECTION - the controller identified the right hazard via the wrong mechanism): in the LIVE instance, already_regressed is NOT what stops the re-page - the WINDOW DRAIN is. Replaying the 1-pass-then-dead shape forward with class banked each night: 07-26 REGRESSION (escalates), then 07-27..07-31 all GAP, because the lucky pass fell out of W=5 and GAP is exempt - already_regressed is never consulted. Separately confirmed against the real history: classify_bench(config_file_parser, tonight=2026-07-31) -> SUSPECTED-FLAKE, consec=4, suppressed BY 07-30's banked class='regression'. So BOTH mechanisms exist and BOTH are load-bearing on different stream shapes (flake-guard :264-265 names both). A fix tested only on the window-drain shape would pass while breaking the guard - which is why M1.2 tests the GUARD shape specifically.

R-D (REJECTION UPHELD, with a stronger reason than the handoff gave): the pass-rate floor is not merely 'silences chronic failures' - it CONTRADICTS A WRITTEN, SHIPPED INVARIANT, flake-guard D2's 'no benchmark that has ever passed goes unpaged past its 3rd consecutive failing night'. A rate floor deletes that guarantee outright. #524's decision_departures rejected a pass-rate disjunct for the adjacent reason (a rate signal cannot distinguish 'we failed to measure the subject' from 'the subject genuinely broke'). The controller was right; the anchor was missing.

metadata.decision_open_question: BOTH SIDES OWN THE FIX, IN ONE PR. The classifier owns the LABEL; the shell owns the MESSAGE; the suppression guard is widened and becomes an explicitly tested invariant. WHY NOT SHELL-ONLY (the controller's leaning): :674 banks verdict.label.lower() into ~/.ailang/state/nightly-eval-history.jsonl, the SOLE input to every future window and escalation count. Shell-only leaves the machine-readable contract asserting 'regression' for a benchmark that was never solid - the exact polluted-trend-input failure #524 spent a milestone remediating, and data whose value is knowingly wrong (CLAUDE.md section 2). WHY NOT CLASSIFIER-ONLY: F-1, MEASURED - the shell drops unrecognised labels silently, so chronic failures go from mislabelled-but-visible to INVISIBLE. THE SUPPRESSION INVARIANT, TESTABLE: PAGING_CLASSES = {'regression','sustained-failure'} ('regression' retained for pre-fix rows, R-4); consecutive_failures returns already_paged (renamed from already_regressed) = any valid night in the current all-fail run whose banked class is in PAGING_CLASSES. A BENCHMARK PAGES AT MOST ONCE PER ALL-FAIL RUN, for both label kinds and across the pre/post-fix boundary. LABEL VOCABULARY AFTER THE FIX (5 labels; REGRESSION narrows, one is added): REGRESSION = window solid (passes==trials) then all-fail tonight -> --type bug + 1 Discord ping; SUSTAINED-FAILURE (new) = K=3 all-fail run with a NON-solid window -> --type bug, NO Discord ping; SUSPECTED-FLAKE -> --type note; GAP -> --type note, STILL EXEMPT from escalation (R-A); INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY -> summary line. NO DISCORD PING FOR SUSTAINED-FAILURE is deliberate and tested (M2.3): the ping's text is 'benchmarks that previously passed now fail' and a sustained failure is the ABSENCE of a change; the ping means 'something broke tonight', the bug means 'this deserves a triage slot' - keeping them separate is the whole point of the sprint. Side benefit: once escalations leave the REGRESSION branch that ping's wording becomes true again for the first time. SUSTAINED-FAILURE carries escalated_from in TSV field 7 and REGRESSION now ALWAYS carries '-' there, so the dead `if [[ "$ESCALATED" != "-" ]]` branch at :515-517 is REMOVED rather than left to rot.
metadata.top_risk: R-1 THE RE-PAGE TRAP (measured, not theorised): renaming the escalated label without teaching consecutive_failures about the new banked class turns 'pages once' into 'pages every night'. Simulated over a stream whose lucky pass stays inside W=5 at the escalation boundary (solid 07-24, 1/2 on 07-25, all-fail after) - TODAY: 07-26 flake, 07-27 flake, 07-28 REGRESSION(pages), 07-29 flake(suppressed), 07-30 flake(suppressed), 07-31 GAP = 1 page. NAIVE RENAME: 07-28/07-29/07-30 all SUSTAINED-FAILURE = 3 PAGES. Every existing test passes under the naive rename except F-3's list, so this MUST be a named new test (M1.2), not a hoped-for regression catch. R-2 THE VANISHING TRAP: see F-1; gated by M2.1 + M3.2. R-3 SUPPRESSING EVERYTHING: a fix that quiets the genuine solid-window break is a regression, not a fix - gated by M1.4 (synthetic 10/10 -> break, same night) and M1.5 (the REAL higher_order_functions 07-26 control from #483 / iteration 113); NEITHER may change. R-4 MIGRATION: live history already has class='regression' rows written by ESCALATIONS (config_file_parser 07-29 and 07-30, verified in P6); if the guard only recognises the new string those rows stop suppressing and the live instance RE-PAGES TOMORROW - the guard must accept both strings (M1.3).
